# GraspNet-baseline

<div class="gp-chips"><span class="gp-chip" title="Seed-based skeleton: GraspNet-baseline, GSNet, Scale-Balanced-Grasp, EconomicGrasp, FineGrasp">Seed-based skeleton</span> <span class="gp-chip" title="GraspNet-1Billion: A Large-Scale Benchmark for General Object Grasping">CVPR 2020</span> <span class="gp-chip">depth input</span> <span class="gp-chip gp-chip--ok" title="stage by stage against the authors&#x27; code, the same weights loaded into both: tests/integration/test_baseline_parity.py">equal to the reference ✓</span> <span class="gp-chip gp-chip--ok" title="the authors&#x27; checkpoint, converted and scored on whole test splits; nothing trained here yet">authors&#x27; weights scored here</span></div>

From the point cloud of a depth image, it keeps 1024 PointNet++ seeds, scores 300 approach views per seed and predicts score, in-plane angle, width and tolerance at four depths along the best one.

[Paper](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content_CVPR_2020/html/Fang_GraspNet-1Billion_A_Large-Scale_Benchmark_for_General_Object_Grasping_CVPR_2020_paper.html) · [Reference code](https://github.com/graspnet/graspnet-baseline/tree/fb2f089a9515d2a5e433b28b53827c1c914437f2) · [Configs, results and notes](https://github.com/Daeda1used/GraspPanda/blob/main/configs/graspnet_baseline/README.md)

## Run GraspNet-baseline in five minutes {#run-in-five-minutes}

Four steps from the authors' checkpoint to grasps. A [test](https://github.com/Daeda1used/GraspPanda/blob/main/tests/unit/test_method_quickstart.py) parses each command and runs the demo and the Python code on a toy detector of the method's family.

### 1. Get the weights {#run-weights}

GraspPanda publishes no weights for GraspNet-baseline: the file to download is the authors' checkpoint, under its licence. Download [`checkpoint-rs.tar`](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1hd0G8LN6tRpi4742XOTEisbTXNZ-1jmk/view?usp=sharing) (Google Drive) and convert it once, from the root of a GraspPanda checkout:

```bash
python -m tools.convert_checkpoint checkpoint-rs.tar baseline_realsense.pth \
    --source-format graspnet-baseline --camera realsense
```

??? note "Licence, checksum and what the converter writes"

    - **Licence**: GraspNet-Baseline Software License Agreement (non-commercial research use only)
    - **SHA-256** of the download: `60680087c61cba2b6791614fef1519071e294f6dcaf99b3f581bb95f7c51a868`
    - **What the converter writes**: `baseline_realsense.pth`, every tensor of the downloaded file under the name of the module that plays its role here, no value changed, with a note of the file it came from. A tensor left over or missing stops the conversion with a report; nothing is ever loaded partially. The converter is a tool of the repository; it is not installed with the package.

### 2. Grasps on the example scene {#run-demo}

```bash
grasppanda demo graspnet_baseline/graspnet-baseline_pointnet2_g1b-realsense_18e \
    --weights baseline_realsense.pth --example --collision-filter
```

`--example` is a synthetic table-top scene shipped with GraspPanda: no dataset, no download. **10.5 s** for the whole command, 285 grasps kept (one NVIDIA RTX A6000 shared with other jobs).

??? note "What it prints and writes, and every measured run"

    The command prints the config and its hash, how the weights loaded (every tensor matched, none missing), the test pipeline, the cloud, how many grasps the model predicted and how many the collision filter left (the config's variant `cd`: `ModelFreeCollisionFilter`), and the ten best grasps. It writes into `work_dirs/graspnet-baseline_pointnet2_g1b-realsense_18e/demo/`:

    - `grasps.npy`: the grasps that are left, `(G, 17)` float32 in the GraspNet layout, best first, camera frame, metres;
    - `grasps.png` and `grasps.gif`: the cloud with the 30 best grasps, still and swinging around the scene;
    - `example/`: the scene as files (`depth.png`, `rgb.png`, `mask.png`, `intrinsics.txt`).

    Measured with the authors' checkpoint, converted: **10.5 s** for the whole command; 20,000 points to the model, sampled from 316,254 in the workspace; 880 grasps predicted, 285 left after ModelFreeCollisionFilter (2026-10-15, commit `ea6268b`, one NVIDIA RTX A6000 shared with other jobs).


### 3. From Python, a browser or your camera {#run-anywhere}

=== "Python"

    ```python
    from grasppanda import GraspInferencer
    from grasppanda.apis import example_scene
    scene = example_scene()  # the scene of --example
    inferencer = GraspInferencer(
        "graspnet_baseline/graspnet-baseline_pointnet2_g1b-realsense_18e",
        "baseline_realsense.pth")
    grasps = inferencer(
        depth=scene.depth, intrinsics=scene.intrinsics,
        depth_scale=scene.depth_scale, mask=scene.mask,
        table_from_camera=scene.table_from_camera, collision_filter=True,
    )
    print(len(grasps), grasps.sort_by_score().to_graspnet_array()[:3])
    ```

    It runs the demo's pipeline on the demo's scene and returns its 285 grasps. `mask=` stands in for the segmentation the config crops the workspace with; on your camera, pass a mask or `workspace=(xmin, ymin, zmin, xmax, ymax, zmax)` in metres. More: [From Python](../user_guides/inference.md#from-python).

=== "Browser"

    ```bash
    # ~/grasppanda_weights: the folder that holds baseline_realsense.pth
    grasppanda explore --weights-dir ~/grasppanda_weights
    ```

    Open <http://127.0.0.1:8765/> and choose GraspNet-baseline in the **Run** tab: `baseline_realsense.pth` is chosen for you by its name. Keep the example scene or upload a depth image with its intrinsics, and press *Run*: the page shows the picture, the best ten grasps, the counts through the post-processing and the command that does the same in a terminal. The server listens on your machine only and downloads nothing: [Run in the browser](../user_guides/inference.md#run-in-the-browser).

=== "Your camera"

    ```bash
    grasppanda demo graspnet_baseline/graspnet-baseline_pointnet2_g1b-realsense_18e \
        --weights baseline_realsense.pth \
        --depth work_dirs/graspnet-baseline_pointnet2_g1b-realsense_18e/demo/example/depth.png \
        --intrinsics work_dirs/graspnet-baseline_pointnet2_g1b-realsense_18e/demo/example/intrinsics.txt \
        --workspace -0.25 -0.2 0.35 0.25 0.2 0.8 \
        --collision-filter --out work_dirs/camera
    ```

    The scene files of step 2 stand in for a camera. GraspNet-baseline was trained on clouds cropped around the objects; on a camera image, `--workspace` (a box in the camera frame, metres) or `--mask` does that crop. Units, frames, the depth scale and the intrinsics: [Your own camera](../user_guides/inference.md#your-own-camera).

### 4. A first number on the benchmark {#run-test}

With GraspNet-1Billion on disk ([Datasets](../user_guides/datasets.md)), score every 64th frame of the seen test scenes, 120 frames:

```bash
grasppanda test graspnet_baseline/graspnet-baseline_pointnet2_g1b-realsense_18e \
    --weights baseline_realsense.pth \
    --opts data.test.dataset.split=test_seen data.test.dataset.frame_step=64 \
    evaluation.num_workers=4
```

Measured with the authors' checkpoint, converted: AP 32.60 without the collision filter and 48.67 with it, within 0.77 AP of the whole split.

??? note "What it prints, and every measured run against the whole split"

    It prints AP, AP0.8 and AP0.4 for every variant of the config, `raw` (the predictions as they are) and `cd` (with the collision filter), and writes a result record per variant into the run directory under `work_dirs/`. Testing needs no derived asset; the evaluator extracts a cache from the dataset's object models the first time it runs, which the times below do not include.

    <div class="gp-matrix" markdown>

    | Weights, provenance | Collision filter | AP, 120 frames of test_seen | AP, whole seen split | Difference | Wall time, commit |
    |---|---|---|---|---|---|
    | the authors' checkpoint, converted, `author-ckpt` | off | 32.60 | 32.64 ([record](https://github.com/Daeda1used/GraspPanda/blob/main/configs/graspnet_baseline/records/graspnet-baseline_pointnet2_g1b-realsense_18e_author-ckpt_test_raw.json)) | −0.04 | 35 s, `ea6268b` |
    |  | on | 48.67 | 47.90 ([record](https://github.com/Daeda1used/GraspPanda/blob/main/configs/graspnet_baseline/records/graspnet-baseline_pointnet2_g1b-realsense_18e_author-ckpt_test_cd.json)) | +0.77 |  |

    </div>

    Provenance: `author-ckpt`, the authors' checkpoint, evaluated by GraspPanda. Inputs: the workspace is cropped around the ground-truth segmentation (`gt_assisted: workspace`), as in the reference. On these 120 frames the AP is within 0.77 AP of the whole split, so the subset tells you quickly whether your installation gives what the records say; it is not a benchmark number. Measured on 2026-10-15 on one NVIDIA RTX A6000 shared with other jobs.

    The machine: one NVIDIA RTX A6000 (48 GB) shared with other jobs, an AMD EPYC 7262 with OMP_NUM_THREADS=3; Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.7.1 with CUDA 11.8, spconv 2.3.8.

| authors' weights | on | 47.90 | 42.70 | 16.98 | [record](https://github.com/Daeda1used/GraspPanda/blob/main/configs/graspnet_baseline/records/graspnet-baseline_pointnet2_g1b-realsense_18e_author-ckpt_test_cd.json) |

</div>

??? note "Where these numbers come from"

    - **The status of these numbers**: authors' weights scored here, the authors' checkpoint, converted and scored on whole test splits; nothing trained here yet.
    - **reported**: reference repository README, "In repo" (collision threshold 0.01); paper, as quoted in the reference repository README ("In paper").
    - **authors' weights, scored here**: the authors' checkpoint, converted and run through `grasppanda test` on every frame of the test split; the record holds the per-scene values, the config hash and the hashes of code and weights.
    - **Inputs**: workspace crop from the ground-truth segmentation, as in the reference (gt_assisted: workspace).
    - Other cameras, GraspClutter6D and what is known about each gap: [the README](https://github.com/Daeda1used/GraspPanda/blob/main/configs/graspnet_baseline/README.md#results-on-graspnet-1billion); every method side by side: [Model zoo](../model_zoo.md).

??? note "How to swap, and how to read these lists"

    Swap one option in with a single line, or list the options of a slot:

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose graspnet_baseline/graspnet-baseline_pointnet2_g1b-realsense_18e \
        --set <slot>=<option> -o swap.yaml
    grasppanda compose graspnet_baseline/graspnet-baseline_pointnet2_g1b-realsense_18e --list <slot>
    ```

    The summary table:

    - **Composes**: the options the config check accepts under GraspNet-baseline, the one it ships included. *needs consent*: an option it holds back until you accept the code it downloads (the row says how), neither accepted nor refused. *no record*: never composed; the row says why.
    - **Refused**: the options the config check refuses under GraspNet-baseline; each row gives the first sentence of the reason. For losses, both columns count the terms (or sets of terms) a preset was tried on.
    - **Runs here**: the swaps whose probe trained on real frames under GraspNet-baseline without an error, out of every option tried there as a swap: a refusal counts, the option the method ships does not, and a loss preset is one option. [Does it run?](../advanced_guides/measured_combinations.md#the-answer) counts the same way.

    The lists of each slot:

    - **Runs**: the methods under which the swap trained on real frames without an error, out of every method it is a swap under; the methods that ship the option are *own* and not counted. Who is left out, and why, stands under the chip, or below the table when it is long. Measured: 20 training iterations on 8 RealSense frames of GraspNet-1Billion (one scene), seed 0, one run per cell; nothing was measured on GraspClutter6D or on Kinect frames.
    - **Trains like shipped**: trained 250 iterations beside the component the method ships, its losses fall as theirs do, out of the methods it was compared under; a method under which the swap did not run, or where it trained on a schedule of its own, is named and not counted. Level 2 needs *runs*, not *learns*: a term flat after 20 iterations can fall by 250. Measured: 250 iterations on 8 RealSense frames of GraspNet-1Billion (one scene), seed 0, at a constant learning rate (FineGrasp: its own warm-up), beside the method as shipped trained the same way twice.
    - **Under GraspNet-baseline**: ✓ when it reached every level here; *level ? (as shipped)* when GraspNet-baseline as shipped does not reach that level either (a note below the table says why), so the level says nothing about the option; else the level it missed and why (*composes*, *runs*, *learns*, *predicts*), or why it was refused.

    The levels, the refusal kinds and the thresholds: [How we measure](../evidence/index.md); every record: [Does it run?](../advanced_guides/measured_combinations.md#measured-classes); every comparison at level 2: [Does it train like the shipped component?](../advanced_guides/learns_like_reference.md).

??? note "How this port differs from the reference"

    - One model instance trains and predicts.
    - Losses are means over the supervised entries (the reference adds 1e-6 to the count),
      and zero, not NaN, when nothing is supervised.
    - Validation uses the `val_dev` scenes, not `test_seen`.

    How it was checked, stage by stage: `tests/integration/test_baseline_parity.py` and [the README](https://github.com/Daeda1used/GraspPanda/blob/main/configs/graspnet_baseline/README.md).
